nodes.summary: Let $f$ map each letter of the three-letter alphabet $\{a, b, c\}$ to a finite word over a set $T$, and extend $f$ to words by concatenation, $f(x_1 \cdots x_n) = f(x_1) \cdots f(x_n)$. Then $f$ maps every square-free word over $\{a, b, c\}$ to a square-free word if and only if it maps every square-free word over $\{a, b, c\}$ of length at most $5$ to a square-free word.
nodes.title: Crochemore's square-freeness test

nodes.summary: An infinite word $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ is square-free if it contains no two adjacent equal nonempty blocks: for all $i \ge 0$ and all $k \ge 1$ there is some $j < k$ with $u_{i+j} \ne u_{i+k+j}$.
nodes.title: Square-free infinite word

nodes.summary: An infinite word $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ over the ternary alphabet is a square-free infinite ternary word if it is square-free as an infinite word.
nodes.title: Square-free infinite ternary word

nodes.summary: A finite word $w$ is square-free if and only if, for every prefix $s$ of a suffix of $w$ and every nonempty prefix $x$ of $s$, we have $s \ne xx$, where $xx$ denotes the concatenation of $x$ with itself.
nodes.title: Square-freeness via prefixes of suffixes

nodes.summary: A finite word $w$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ is square-free if no factor of $w$ is a square, where a factor of $w$ is a word $s$ with $w = psq$ for some words $p$ and $q$, and a square is a word $xx$ with $x$ nonempty.
nodes.title: Square-free finite word

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a finite word $w$ over the ternary alphabet is a square-free ternary word of length $n$ if $w$ is square-free and $w$ has length exactly $n$.
nodes.title: Square-free ternary words of length $n$

nodes.summary: A word $w$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a square if $w = xx$ for some nonempty word $x$, where $xx$ denotes the concatenation of $x$ with itself.
nodes.title: Square word

nodes.summary: If a finite word $v$ is square-free and $u$ is a factor of $v$, that is, $v = puq$ for some words $p$ and $q$, then $u$ is square-free.
nodes.title: Factors of square-free words are square-free

nodes.summary: The ternary alphabet is the set $\{0, 1, 2\}$ of natural numbers less than $3$; its three letters play the role of $a$, $b$ and $c$.
nodes.title: The ternary alphabet for square-free words

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
